result.tail:
100% grass-fed on milk means the cows ate grass and hay, never grain. 
     Reduced-fat, low-fat and skim are all whole milk with milkfat removed. They come from skimming cream off before homogenization and adding less back, never from adding water. The fat carries the flavor and most of the fullness. Dairy fat research is mixed, so the call rests on the processing, the checkable part. Grass-fed and pasture milk is a further layer, separate from the fat. 
     Reduced-fat (2%) / low-fat (1%) / skim 
     Progressively more milk fat removed. 
     A2 
     The herd was tested and carries only the A2 beta-casein variant. A breed-genetics claim, not a welfare or processing one. 
     Pasteurized 
     Briefly heated to kill pathogens. The standard process. 
     Ultra-pasteurized / UHT 
     Much hotter for a shorter time. Long shelf life, changed flavor, resists culturing. 
     Homogenized 
     Fat broken into droplets so cream never rises. Not a heat process. 
     Cream-top / non-homogenized 
     Cream separates and rises. Still pasteurized. 
     Vat pasteurized 
     Held at 145°F for 30 minutes; also printed as low-temperature pasteurized. 
     Ultra-pasteurized 
     Heated to about 280°F for about 2 seconds. 
     Vat, or low-temp, pasteurizing holds milk at 145°F for 30 minutes; regular gets 161°F for 15 seconds. 
     Whole vs. reduced 
     If you can’t get raw: low-temp pasteurized, organic, 100% grass-fed whole milk.
